gen-gf-phudu-gf-snippet: Phudu's curves open generously at every terminal, drawn with the plain, pressure-free line of a ballpoint, which gives it real attitude. Snippet, a plain sans, is the quieter one, with wire-bent letters.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-sour-gummy: Sour Gummy keeps its gaps wide so tiny sizes stay crisp. Phudu's thread-outline strokes carry the loud, rounded display voice above while the sans handles the text.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-source-sans-3: Distinctive is the right word for Phudu, whose strokes run like bent wire and whose curve endings gape open. Source Sans 3 gives that a plain sans partner, with an a whose lower bowl breathes.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-spinnaker: Phudu draws every letter as an outline of one steady thickness. Shrink it down and that bold display swagger fades, while Spinnaker, a sans-serif, keeps its counters connected to the outside and holds up at text sizes.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-stick: Chunky, marker-bold personality up top, with curves that open wide at every terminal and never press harder anywhere. Make Phudu small and it loses that punch, whereas Stick's tubelike lines suit text.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-suse: SUSE reads friendly and contemporary, its open bowls tipped toward you like a ladle. Phudu does bold, distinctive display work best, while SUSE does the quiet job of carrying sentences.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-suse-mono: SUSE Mono gives every letter extra room on both sides, with open curves and clear gaps. Over a long passage it feels approachable and unhurried, while Phudu's marker-tip lines make the heading louder.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-tajawal: Phudu's uninterrupted line width on every letter, with curves that open generously at their ends, is what makes it stand out. Tajawal, a clean sans-serif with a c like a broad open hook, reads smoothly over a long stretch.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-tasa-explorer: TASA Explorer reads clean and approachable, its curves ending like brush strokes lifted early. Phudu is best at bold display, with no hairlines or swells, while TASA Explorer does the steady text work.
